map.诉讼时效计算 使用指南: Statute of Limitations Calculator User Guide
map.根据权利受到侵害或知道权利受损的日期，计算诉讼时效届满日，提示剩余可主张权利的时: Computes when the statute of limitations expires from the date the right was infringed or became known, and shows the time left to enforce it.
map.普通时效：权利受侵害 / 知道之日 2021-01-01，普通诉讼时效 3 年，: Ordinary limitation: the right was harmed or became known on 2021-01-01, so the 3-year ordinary period expires 2024-01-01.
map.时效中断：起算 2020-06-01，2022-06-01 提起诉讼中断，自中断: Interruption: the period starts 2020-06-01; filing suit on 2022-06-01 interrupts it, and 3 years is recomputed from the interruption date, expiring 2025-06-01.
map.时效中止：起算 2021-01-01（届满 2024-01-01），2023-1: Suspension: the period starts 2021-01-01 (expiring 2024-01-01); force majeure occurs 2023-10-01 and the obstacle ends 2024-02-01, so it is suspended 123 days and expiry is extended to 2024-05-03.
map.算例：3 年普通时效与中止: Worked example: the 3-year ordinary period with suspension
map.：起算日 2021-01-01，普通 3 年 → 届满 2024-01-01。若: : starting 2021-01-01 with an ordinary 3 years gives expiry 2024-01-01. If force majeure occurs in the last 6 months (2023-10-01) and ends 2024-02-01, the suspension is 2024-02-01 − 2023-10-01 = 123 days, so expiry moves to 2024-01-01 + 123 days = 2024-05-03. In the interruption case, 3 years is recomputed from the interruption date (such as 2022-06-01).
map.时效中断与中止有何区别？: What Is the Difference Between Interruption and Suspension of the Limitation Period?
map.中断因起诉、一方提出要求或同意履行而发生，从中断时起重新计算；中止因不可抗力等障: Interruption happens on filing suit, a demand by one party, or agreement to perform, and the period restarts from the interruption. Suspension happens when an obstacle such as force majeure occurs in the last 6 months, and the limitation expires 6 months after the obstacle ends (this tool approximates by simply extending the suspension days).
map.最长 20 年保护期如何起算？: How Is the 20-Year Maximum Protection Period Counted?
map.自权利受到损害之日起算，不适用“知道或应当知道”规则；超过 20 年法院不予保护: Counted from the day the right was harmed, without the "knew or should have known" rule; beyond 20 years a court gives no protection, though special cases may be extended.
